name: Zscaler
product_focus: ZIA, ZPA, ZDX, Zero Trust SASE
evidence_summary: Sources evidence Zscaler ZIA/ZPA integration with SD-WAN and Zscaler Zero Trust SASE with fresh SD-WAN approach; historically SSE-led.
cost_model: Quote-based subscription; typically per-user/workload/location modules; SD-WAN integrations may add partner/vendor cost.
key_differentiators: Category leader in SSE with ZIA, ZPA and ZDX; widely adopted as the security layer in best-of-breed SASE architectures.
Strong ecosystem of SD-WAN partners (Cisco, others) for buyers wanting Zscaler security with a separate SD-WAN platform.
Mature Zero Trust platform with substantial enterprise deployment history.
best_fit_for: Enterprises selecting best-of-breed SSE alongside a separate SD-WAN platform.
Security-driven SASE strategies where the SSE layer is the primary architectural decision.
Buyers consolidating multiple security point solutions onto a single SSE vendor.
watch_outs: Historically SSE-led; native SD-WAN capability is less mature than dedicated SD-WAN platforms (validate path selection, QoS and packet loss in RFP).
Premium pricing; typically per-user/workload/location with security modules adding cost.
Buyers needing one vendor for both SD-WAN and security may prefer a converged platform (Cato, FortiSASE, Prisma).
verification_notes: Re-verified 2026-07-29 against named primary sources. Every graded fact carries a source, a tier and a verbatim quote confirmed present on the cited page by an independent check. Industry, region, organisation-size and pricing evidence was sourced on the same basis. Facts that could not be sourced are published as unknown with the reason. The value_tier field is a Netify assessment of relative cost position, not a supplier claim: most of this market publishes no price. Sources found and rejected are listed at tier 4.

ai_capability.note: AI-powered phishing and C2 detection; ZDX Copilot for digital experience.

resilience.note: 160+ PoP cloud with service continuity features across regions.

profile.platform_architecture: Zscaler runs the Zero Trust Exchange, a security cloud of 160+ PoPs processing hundreds of billions of transactions daily. Users, workloads and devices connect to the nearest PoP where policy is enforced; there is no network to join, which is the architectural point. Zscaler does not ship SD-WAN appliances: branch connectivity pairs the Exchange with third-party SD-WAN, and Zscaler Zero Trust Branch options reduce branch hardware needs.
profile.security_sase: ZIA (internet and SaaS security) and ZPA (private application access) are category-defining: SWG, CASB, DLP, sandboxing, browser isolation and the most widely deployed ZTNA in the market, with AI-powered phishing and command-and-control detection. Zscaler Digital Experience (ZDX) adds user experience monitoring. For SSE capability depth and scale, Zscaler sets the benchmark most rivals are measured against.
profile.service_support_channel: Strong UK presence direct and through security partners and carriers; BT, Vodafone and global SIs deliver managed Zscaler. Deployment is agent and tunnel based with substantial professional services ecosystems. Support tiers run to 24x7 with TAM options; operating Zscaler well still demands skilled policy ownership in-house or via partner.
profile.commercials_verdict: Per-user subscription bundles (Editions) that are quote based and premium; transaction volumes justify it for large estates. The Netify verdict: shortlist Zscaler when a zero trust programme leads the agenda, when SSE depth and global PoP scale matter, and when SD-WAN is solved separately. Small organisations and single-site estates are outside its sweet spot.

vendor_faqs.a: Not entirely. Zscaler replaces the security stack and removes much branch security hardware, while site-to-site connectivity still wants an SD-WAN layer; common pairings include Catalyst, EdgeConnect, Fortinet and VeloCloud feeding traffic into the Exchange.

vendor_faqs.q: What is the difference between ZIA and ZPA?
vendor_faqs.a: ZIA secures traffic to internet and SaaS destinations (SWG, CASB, DLP, sandboxing). ZPA brokers least-privilege access to private applications without placing users on the network, replacing VPN concentrators. Most deployments run both.

vendor_faqs.q: Is Zscaler suitable for mid-market UK organisations?
vendor_faqs.a: Yes via managed routes: BT, Vodafone and UK MSPs wrap Zscaler with deployment and operations. Direct DIY suits organisations with capable security teams; smaller estates often find the licensing premium harder to justify.

shortlist_summary: Zscaler are the category leader in SSE, with ZIA covering secure internet access, ZPA handling private application access, and ZDX providing digital experience monitoring. Typically shortlisted as the security layer in best-of-breed SASE architectures, often evaluated alongside a separate SD-WAN platform rather than as a converged single-vendor option. For organisations already invested in Zscaler for SSE, ZDX's experience monitoring is often the deciding factor on whether to extend the investment.
cost_note: Per-user Editions, premium priced; transaction scale justifies it for large estates.
uk_basis: No UK HQ (US). UK PoPs in the Zero Trust Exchange; delivered direct or via UK partners and carriers.

f01_fully_managed_service.quote: We partner with service providers to develop comprehensive managed offers that leverage the Zero Trust Exchange, our industry-leading security platform, to enable profitable managed service provider business models.
f01_fully_managed_service.note: Zscaler operates the platform itself and sells one first-party managed service (Zscaler MDR, security operations). On its own partner page the comprehensive managed offer is built and delivered by service provider partners, not by Zscaler. No Zscaler page was found describing Zscaler itself designing, deploying, changing and reporting on a customer's end-to-end service, so graded partial rather than yes.

f03_co_managed_service.quote: Human-led, hands-on-keyboard response acts as an extension of your security team and ensures threats can be mitigated even when your team is unavailable, 24x7x365.
f03_co_managed_service.note: Zscaler runs the platform as SaaS with a contractual SLA while the customer retains policy authoring, and MDR is explicitly positioned as an extension of the customer's own team, which is the shared-responsibility pattern. However no Zscaler page read set out a formal co-managed service definition with a documented split of change rights between Zscaler and the customer, so graded partial.

f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.quote: The Multi-Tenant Portal has long been the cornerstone for Managed Service Providers (MSPs) and large-scale enterprises to oversee multiple Zscaler instances.
f04_multi_tenant_msp_white_label_support.note: Tenant isolation, cross-tenant pivoting and centralised delegated administration through ZIdentity are documented for MSPs. Nothing was found on Zscaler's own pages evidencing branded or white-label portals under the partner's own brand, and the definition requires that. The definitive partner portal documentation on help.zscaler.com could not be read because it is a JavaScript-only page (register 23). Graded partial for that reason.

f05_professional_services_and_migration_.quote: Review current Zscaler implementation and operations, provide leading practices, recommendations and remediation plan
f05_professional_services_and_migration_.note: Zscaler publishes tiered deployment packages (Essential through Enterprise Plus) covering architecture and design, pilot user test plans, phased site rollout, production support and education credits, plus separate datasheets for ZIA policy creation and migration and for resident engineers. The datasheet is largely tabular, so the quote is the longest continuous prose string available. Confidence medium because the source is undated and table-formatted, which raises the risk of line-break differences on re-fetch.

f07_lifecycle_management.note: Not found in public sources reviewed. The Zero Trust Branch product page, the Zero Trust SD-WAN datasheet and the Zero Trust Branch datasheet were all read specifically for hardware replacement or RMA, firmware upgrade, patching, renewals and end-of-life statements. The datasheets list appliance models (ZT 400, ZT 600, ZT 800, ZT 8010) and single-touch provisioning but say nothing about who owns firmware upgrades, hardware replacement or end-of-life planning. Absence is not being treated as a no.

f17_cellular_and_5g_support.quote: Devices use Zscaler SIMs to steer traffic securely to the Zero Trust Exchange with no need for additional software.
f17_cellular_and_5g_support.note: Zscaler Cellular provides Zscaler-issued SIMs that carry cellular IoT and mobile device traffic into the Zero Trust Exchange, which covers SIM provisioning and management. The definition also asks for 4G and 5G as primary or failover WAN transport with modem and signal monitoring. Neither the Cellular product page nor the July 2025 cellular press release names 4G, 5G or LTE, the private 5G page concerns securing a customer's private 5G core rather than WAN transport, and the Zero Trust SD-WAN datasheet contains no cellular uplink specification. Graded partial on that gap.

f19_public_cloud_gateways.quote: Zscaler already operates 160+ data centers and is present in most countries.
f19_public_cloud_gateways.note: This is Zscaler's own infrastructure, not a resold third party's, so yes rather than partner_integrated. The reference architecture confirms Zscaler deploys its own ZIA Service Edge devices into those data centres and that users are always directed to the nearest one for traffic processing, which is security enforcement and SaaS access delivered as the vendor's own cloud service.

f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.quote: ZIA Private Service Edge and ZIA Virtual Service Edge devices extend the Zscaler cloud into your data center.
f20_private_pops_dedicated_pops.note: Directly meets the definition: customer-hosted and dedicated deployments exist alongside the shared multi-tenant Public Service Edges. The March 2026 sovereignty press release additionally describes Private Service Edges as single-tenant, customer-hosted, and Zscaler-managed appliances, plus dedicated control and logging planes in six countries, which covers the sovereign case.

f21_private_global_backbone.quote: Direct peering with major internet and SaaS providers and public cloud destinations ensures the fastest traffic path possible.
f21_private_global_backbone.note: No claim of a vendor-owned or vendor-controlled inter-region backbone was found on any Zscaler page read. The published architecture is peering-based: the reference architecture states many data centres are in internet exchange peering points with other cloud infrastructure and application providers, such as Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. The only global-WAN backbone material found was a 2023 blog describing the Teridion Liquid Network, which is a third party's infrastructure and is Tier 3 corroboration only (register 20), so it cannot support a grade. Graded not_primary rather than unknown because the vendor's own architecture documents describe an internet-and-peering model, but confidence is low since this is read off architecture description rather than an explicit vendor statement about backbone ownership.

f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.quote: The SaaS will be available to accept Customer's Transactions and Sessions 99.999% of the total hours during every month Customer uses the SaaS
f26_sla_backed_service_fabric.note: Zscaler publishes a contractual SLA schedule covering availability by product (99.999% for ZIA, ZPA, ZDX and Zero Trust Device Segmentation or Microsegmentation; 99.99% for DNS-based guest WiFi; 99.9% for Risk360, DSPM, Cellular, MDR and others), a latency commitment, and tiered support response times (15 minutes P1 on Premium Support Advanced, 2 hours P1 on Standard Support). That is contractual rather than best-effort.

f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.quote: Built on a cloud native platform, a zero trust firewall protects web and non-web traffic for all users, apps, locations, and clouds.
f27_integrated_next_generation_firewall.note: Native Zscaler technology, not a resold or bundled third party, so yes rather than partner_integrated. The ZIA datasheet corroborates the combined firewall and IPS function with the line Zscaler Firewall & cloud IPS: Extend industry-leading protection to all ports and protocols, and replace edge and branch firewalls with a cloud native platform. The cloud firewall page also cites always-on cloud IPS with custom signatures and native TLS/SSL decryption. URL filtering and malware inspection are delivered by the same ZIA platform rather than a separate appliance.

f33_data_loss_prevention.quote: Deliver high-performance DLP inspection across web and email data.
f33_data_loss_prevention.note: Native inline DLP with content classification (LLM classification, EDM, IDM, OCR and regex) and blocking of risky access across web, GenAI, endpoints, email, SaaS and IaaS. The ZIA datasheet corroborates with Cloud Data Loss Prevention (DLP): Protect data in motion with full inline inspection and advanced measures like exact data match (EDM). Alerting and exception workflow detail was not separately quotable from the pages read, but the classify, inspect and block elements of the definition are met.

f40_managed_service_assurance.quote: Human-led, hands-on-keyboard response acts as an extension of your security team and ensures threats can be mitigated even when your team is unavailable, 24x7x365.
f40_managed_service_assurance.note: Zscaler MDR provides 24/7 monitoring, investigation and response with human analysts, and the SLA schedule commits MDR response within 10 minutes of a Zscaler analyst confirming a threat, plus 24 x 7 x 365 support access across tiers. However the MDR page and brochure were both read for root cause analysis ownership, formal escalation procedure and structured service reviews or change governance, and none of those were stated, and no vendor-run NOC (as distinct from SOC) was evidenced. Graded partial for those gaps.

delivery_model.quote: We partner with service providers to develop comprehensive managed offers that leverage the Zero Trust Exchange, our industry-leading security platform, to enable profitable managed service provider business models.
delivery_model.note: Zscaler authors and operates its own SaaS security platform (technology vendor) and also sells a Zscaler-delivered managed service in the form of Zscaler MDR. End-to-end managed SASE or network service to enterprises is, on Zscaler's own partner page, positioned as something service provider partners build on top of the Zero Trust Exchange. Graded both on that basis.

underlay_ownership.quote: Direct peering with major internet and SaaS providers and public cloud destinations ensures the fastest traffic path possible.
underlay_ownership.note: No Zscaler page read states that Zscaler owns physical circuits or core routing; the published model is that customers forward their own internet or MPLS transport to the nearest Service Edge, with Zscaler peering at internet exchanges. The one caveat is Zscaler Cellular, where Zscaler supplies its own SIMs riding mobile operator networks, which is a Zscaler-supplied access product rather than circuit ownership. Confidence low because this is read off architecture documents rather than an explicit ownership statement, and no supplier statement was found either confirming or denying circuit ownership.

sse_layer_ownership.quote: Distributed across more than 160 data centers globally, the SSE-based Zero Trust Exchange™ is the world's largest in-line cloud security platform.
sse_layer_ownership.note: Zscaler built and operates its own SSE stack (Zero Trust Exchange, ZIA, ZPA, ZDX, cloud firewall, cloud IPS, DLP) running on Zscaler-operated Service Edge infrastructure in Zscaler data centres. No third-party security vendor is named as the source of the SSE layer on any page read. Zscaler is the vendor that other suppliers resell, rather than a reseller of someone else's stack.

regulatory_documentation.quote: Zscaler compliance enablers are built on foundational programs focusing on data protection and regulatory requirements, including ISO 27001, ISO 27701, SOC 2, and various others.
regulatory_documentation.note: Zscaler operates a dedicated compliance portal naming specific attestations rather than making a general assurance statement, which is why this is documented and not assurance_only. Frameworks found and named on the portal: SOC 2 Type 2, SOC 3, ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27017:2015, ISO/IEC 27018:2019, ISO/IEC 27701, ISO 22301, CSA STAR Level 2, FIPS 140-2, FIPS 140-3, HIPAA, HITRUST, GDPR, PCI DSS, C5, Cyber Essentials Plus, TISAX, ISMAP, IRAP, ENS, MTCS Level 3, NIST 800-53 Rev. 5, G-Cloud, EU-US DPF, Swiss-US DPF, UK Extension to EU-US DPF, CISA Secure-by-Design Pledge, China Cybersecurity Law (CSL), CCCS CSP ITS, DCSO Security Assessment, FSQS, TruSight and CyberVadis Gold. Frameworks specifically looked for and NOT found on the portal listing: DORA, NIS2 and NHS DSPT. FedRAMP was not returned in the portal listing read here; a separate Zscaler press release announcing FedRAMP High authorisation was seen in search results but was not fetched in this task, so it is not cited as evidence.

pop_count.quote: Zscaler already operates 160+ data centers and is present in most countries.
pop_count.note: Value recorded as 160 from the 160+ figure in the March 2026 press release, corroborated by the ZIA datasheet phrase more than 160 data centers globally. Zscaler's own older material states 150+, so the figure is a published floor rather than an exact count. See conflicts. Zscaler counts data centres rather than using the term PoP consistently, although its 2019 press release equates the two.

sla_availability_pct.quote: The SaaS will be available to accept Customer's Transactions and Sessions 99.999% of the total hours during every month Customer uses the SaaS
sla_availability_pct.note: 99.999% applies to ZIA, ZPA, ZDX and Zero Trust Device Segmentation or Microsegmentation. Lower figures apply to other Zscaler products in the same schedule: 99.99% for DNS-based guest WiFi and 99.9% for Posture Control, Risk360, Business Insights, UVM, DSPM, Breach Predictor, EASM, Cellular, MDR and Identity Protection. The ZIA datasheet corroborates with Availability 99.999%, measured by transactions lost. A separate latency commitment of 100 milliseconds or less for the 95th percentile of traffic is also published.

sectors.healthcare.quote: Leverage a HIPAA- and HITECH-compliant zero trust architecture
sectors.healthcare.note: Dedicated healthcare industry page carrying four named healthcare customers with attributed executives: Seattle Children's Hospital (Dr Zafar Chaudry, Chief Digital Officer), Atlantic Health System (Dr Devon Klein), Ramsay Health Care (Julian Zelones) and Keiju Medical Center (Masahiro Kamino). Meets the 'named case study plus dedicated industry page plus published framework' bar several times over. All evidence is vendor-published; no independent verification of the deployments was found.

sectors.financial_services.quote: We embraced security as a journey that ran in parallel with our exploration of our applications, data, and transaction processing.
sectors.financial_services.note: Quote is attributed to Fannie Mae on the dedicated financial services page. Four named customers across three continents: Fannie Mae (US), Hastings Direct (UK insurance), Capitec (South Africa) and L&T Financial Services (India). A second banking landing page corroborates the same set. Regulatory frameworks named on the page include PCI DSS, SOX, NIST CSF and ISO 27001.

sectors.retail_ecommerce.note: No retail or ecommerce industry page exists on the industries index, which lists only banking and financial services, healthcare, US public sector, Australian government, China, education and manufacturing. Retail-looking names (Kingfisher, Belkin International, J&P Cycles, Sunkist) appear in the customers logo wall, but that page carries no per-customer industry labelling and no case study behind those names, so there is nothing to quote. The customer success stories index that would have carried industry filter labels returned 404. Graded unknown rather than partial because the word 'retail' was not found in any sector list or sentence on the pages read.

sectors.manufacturing.quote: Zero trust principles are incredibly relevant to smart factory initiatives.
sectors.manufacturing.note: Quote attributed to Herbert Wegmann, General Manager, Siemens AG, on the dedicated manufacturing industry page. Three further named manufacturers with attributed CISO-level quotes: AkzoNobel (Raffaele Maresca, CISO), Coats (Benjamin Corll, VP of Cybersecurity) and Sanmina (Matt Ramberg, VP of Information Security). Page headline 'Siemens secures digital transformation in modern factory environments' confirms these are full case studies, not logos.

sectors.energy_utilities.note: No energy or utilities industry page on the industries index and the words energy and utilities were not found as a sector label on any page read. NOV, an oilfield equipment company, appears as a named customer on the platform page under the headline 'NOV secures access for 27,000 employees across 60 countries', and Viridor Waste Management and SemGroup Corporation appear in the customer logo wall, but none of these is presented by Zscaler as energy sector evidence. Deliberately not inferring an energy grade from a customer that happens to operate in that industry.

sectors.government_public_sector.quote: Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) and Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) have been FedRAMP Moderate authorized since 2018.
sectors.government_public_sector.note: Strongest sector in the set. Dedicated public sector page plus separate federal, state and local, and Australian government pages. Named agency case studies include the Federal Communications Commission and the State of Oklahoma (34,000 employees across 90+ agencies). Accreditations claimed include FedRAMP JAB-High, FedRAMP Moderate, TIC 3.0 and CJIS, and separately IRAP at PROTECTED for Australia. The FedRAMP claims are independently checkable on the FedRAMP marketplace, which was not done in this task.

sectors.education.quote: Comply with CIPA, StateRAMP, CMMC, and more
sectors.education.note: Dedicated education page sits under the public sector path, not at /industries/education which returns 404. Named institutions with figures: New York City Department of Education (1 million users, 2 million devices), Virginia Commonwealth University (28,000 students), University of South Carolina, and MCNC ('Helps Protect More than 1.1 Million Students and Educators'). The Australian government page separately names CEnet (education, 330K users) and NSW Government Education, so education evidence spans two regions.

sectors.transport_logistics.quote: United Airlines detects and blocks evolving threats
sectors.transport_logistics.note: Graded yes on a named case study rather than a dedicated industry page, so confidence is medium rather than high. The United Airlines story on the platform page carries an attributed quote from Deneen DeFiore, VP and CISO. Air France-KLM, Ocean Shipholdings and Pitney Bowes also appear in the customer logo wall without case studies. There is no transport or logistics industry page, so Zscaler is not marketing to this sector as a named vertical.

sectors.professional_services.note: No professional services industry page and the sector is not named in any list or sentence on the pages read. Intertek, MindTree, AGC Partners and Applied Systems appear in the customer logo wall with no case study or industry label behind them. Nothing quotable, so unknown rather than partial.

sectors.hospitality_leisure.note: No hospitality or leisure industry page and no named hospitality customer or case study found. The closest names in the customer logo wall are sports and entertainment organisations (Houston Rockets, Miami Heat, Village Roadshow, NBC Universal), which are not hospitality or leisure operators in the sense this field measures. No evidence either way.

regions.uk_ireland.quote: 160+ Global data centers, with users in 185 countries
regions.uk_ireland.note: Graded partial with low confidence deliberately. No UK or Ireland specific coverage, points-of-presence or data centre page was found, and the authoritative per-city data centre list at config.zscaler.com is a JavaScript application that could not be read. UK customers do appear: Hastings Direct is a named case study on the financial services page, and British Council, HCA Healthcare UK, Kingfisher and Dairy Crest appear in the customer logo wall. That indicates delivery in the UK but falls short of published regional coverage. No Ireland-specific evidence at all.

regions.europe.quote: Zero trust principles are incredibly relevant to smart factory initiatives.
regions.europe.note: Quote is attributed to Siemens AG (Germany) on the manufacturing page. Graded yes on the strength of multiple named European case studies rather than a published European points-of-presence list, which was not obtainable. European case studies include Siemens AG, AkzoNobel (Netherlands) and Baker & Baker (headline 'Baker & Baker boosts enterprise data security by nearly 90%'); LVMH, Michelin Group, Eramet and Pernod Ricard appear in the logo wall. Confidence medium because coverage is inferred from customer presence plus a global aggregate, not from a regional coverage statement.

regions.north_america.quote: Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) and Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) are both JAB-High authorized.
regions.north_america.note: Strongest region. US federal authorisation at FedRAMP JAB-High is a delivery-grade credential, not a marketing claim, and is backed by named US public sector deployments (FCC, State of Oklahoma, New York City Department of Education) and US healthcare deployments (Seattle Children's Hospital, Atlantic Health System). Zscaler is US-headquartered. No Canada-specific evidence was sought or found.

regions.asia_pacific.quote: The Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange™ has completed its IRAP assessment at PROTECTED, providing details on the implementation, appropriateness, and effectiveness of the system's security controls.
regions.asia_pacific.note: IRAP assessment at PROTECTED is an Australian government scheme credential and is the best region-specific delivery evidence found outside North America. Backed by a long list of named Australian bodies including Services Australia, Australia Post, Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Queensland Government, CENITEX (36,000 users, 450 sites) and CEnet (330K users). Japan is separately evidenced by Keiju Medical Center on the healthcare page, and India by L&T Financial Services on the financial services page.

regions.middle_east_africa.quote: …we're constantly asking ourselves, 'What is the best thing we can do to serve our clients?'
regions.middle_east_africa.note: Quote is attributed to Capitec, a South African bank, on the financial services page. Note the quote begins with an ellipsis character as published, which is part of the verbatim string. Careem, a Middle East mobility operator, appears on the platform page under the headline 'Careem leverages global talent with secure work-from-anywhere'. Graded partial not yes because no MEA coverage page, data centre list or regional accreditation was found, and both data points are single customers rather than a stated coverage claim.

regions.latin_america.note: Actively checked and not found. The company news blog index was searched specifically for Latin America, Brazil and Mexico coverage or expansion announcements and returned nothing. No Latin American customer appears in the customer logo wall, no Spanish or Portuguese language regional page was surfaced, and the investor relations global figure of '160+ Global data centers, with users in 185 countries' is an aggregate that says nothing about the region. The unreadable config.zscaler.com node list would very likely show Latin American cities, so this unknown reflects a retrieval limit, not a claim that coverage is absent.

regions.china_mainland.quote: Zscaler helps multinational organizations provide fast, consistent, reliable, and secure internet connectivity to international websites and SaaS applications, such as Microsoft 365, Salesforce, and ServiceNow, for their employees in mainland China.
regions.china_mainland.note: This clears the bar set for China because it is a specifically named mainland China product (Zscaler China Premium Access) with its own page linked from the industries index, not a generic global claim. Important caveat: the page does not disclose the licensing arrangement, the in-country data centre footprint or the local carrier partner, and a linked technical note ('Zscaler in China | Tech Note') was not retrieved. So the offering is evidenced but the regulatory mechanism behind it is not. A buyer with a China requirement should ask for that tech note. Confidence medium for that reason.

organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.quote: 9.4K+ customers, including 40% of the Forbes Global 2000
organisation_fit.large_global_enterprise.note: Unambiguous. Reinforced across the whole site by the profile of the named case studies: Siemens AG, United Airlines, LVMH, Michelin, Ramsay Health Care (90,000+ employees, 10 countries), NOV (27,000 employees, 60 countries), New York City Department of Education (1 million users). Every case study found was a large or very large organisation. The company FAQ page conflicts, stating 'nearly 8,000 customers around the world' against 9.4K+ on the about and investor pages; recorded per the no-conflict-resolution rule, and the FAQ page appears simply to be stale.

organisation_fit.mid_market.note: Checked deliberately and found nothing. The pricing page names bundles (Essentials Platform marked 'RECOMMENDED', and Zscaler Platform) but does not segment them by organisation size, and the products and solutions hub contains no mid-market or SMB language. No case study of a mid-sized organisation was found; the smallest named deployment encountered was Seattle Children's Hospital at '4,000+ users47 sites4 US states'. The Essentials Platform bundle could plausibly be a mid-market entry point but Zscaler does not describe it that way, and inferring that would be exactly the reasoning this exercise exists to remove.

organisation_fit.small_business.note: No small business or SMB targeting language found on the products hub, the pricing page or the about page. Zscaler does not explicitly say small business is out of scope, so this is unknown rather than not_primary. The observable evidence, a customer base described by Global 2000 penetration and a case study set consisting entirely of large organisations, points away from small business, but there is no published statement to grade against.

published_pricing.note: No price is published that we could quote. The value_tier field on this record is a Netify assessment of relative cost position, not a supplier claim.
